books.section: The Decline of Public Trust in the 1970s

primary_sources: Jimmy Carter, televised address, July 15, 1979 (paraphrased); Torrijos-Carter Treaties, 1977

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Carter's record, 1977-1979

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of President Jimmy Carter's 1976 campaign promise, the Panama Canal treaties of 1977, and his televised address of July 15, 1979. Account drawn from the grounding books (Barron's Ch. 10, Topic 8.14; 5 Steps Ch. 28; Princeton Ch. 12).
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of President Jimmy Carter's record in 1977-1979. Carter won the presidency in 1976 as a Washington outsider who promised, 'I will never lie to you.' In 1977 he signed treaties returning the Panama Canal Zone to Panama by December 31, 1999. On July 15, 1979, in a televised address, he said the country faced a 'crisis of confidence' that went deeper than the energy shortage, and he called for sacrifice and conservation.

stem: The Panama Canal treaties best show which side of Carter's presidency?

options.text: His plan to keep the Panama Canal under American control forever more.
options.misconception: The treaties returned the Canal Zone to Panama by December 31, 1999, the opposite of keeping it forever.

options.text: His outright refusal to negotiate with Panama about the canal at all.
options.misconception: Carter signed treaties with Panama in 1977, so he did negotiate.

options.text: His willingness to accept limits on American power abroad, attacked as giving America away.
His decision to go to war with Panama over control of the canal.
options.misconception: No war was fought over the canal; the treaties were negotiated and ratified by the Senate.

rationales.A: The treaties returned the Canal Zone to Panama by December 31, 1999, the opposite of keeping it forever.
rationales.B: Carter signed treaties with Panama in 1977, so he did negotiate.
rationales.C: Background: The treaties gave up direct control of a strategic asset, and conservatives such as Senators Thurmond and Helms attacked them as surrender.
rationales.D: No war was fought over the canal; the treaties were negotiated and ratified by the Senate.
rationales.general:
1. The passage says the treaties returned the Canal Zone to Panama by 1999.
2. Giving up control of a canal America built is accepting a limit on American power.
3. Background: Conservatives attacked the treaties as giving America away, which is exactly why they matter politically.
Remember: A treaty that gives something up shows a president's sense of limits.
